representations_and_conversion_obligatio.notes: Independently checked the pinned definitions: EuclideanSpace 𝕜 ι is PiLp 2 (constant 𝕜), with distance sqrt(sum coordinate-distance squares); PiLp's function coercion is WithLp.ofLp. Thus Fin n indexes n real coordinates, the 2 is the L2 exponent, and no ordinary max-product metric enters P. Fin.snoc appends at Fin.last n and recovers the first n coordinates at castSucc, including n=0. T003 explicitly requires both inverse identities, the full Euclidean distance identity and the two LipschitzWith 1 bounds (the constant is ℝ≥0). These identify the coordinate-defined YuiCylinder with exactly E×I in both directions. The header defines I as the closed real interval with both endpoints. Metric.ediam is the supremum of pairwise edist and is zero on empties. YuiCost's supremum over a nonempty witness is ediam^s for nonempty members and bottom=0 for empty members; YuiCover imposes precisely union containment and the mesh bound. The guarded infimum over sequences matches countable covers in both directions by enumeration/empty padding; T007's subtype of ℕ also represents finite nonempty families without repeated positive costs. YuiMeasure is the supremum over all positive real scales. The pinned native Hausdorff formula has the same empty-member guard, cost and cover conditions, with positive ENNReal scales. T001 explicitly proves equality after restricting to finite positive scales; the top-scale content cannot enlarge the supremum, and every positive finite extended scale is ofReal of its positive real value. T002 retains normalization and all four critical implications. Native dimH is indeed the ENNReal supremum of nonnegative finite exponents with infinite Borel Hausdorff measure, with the stipulated empty dimension. Positive-exponent ofReal conversions are exact; T007/T008's q>D forces q>0 rather than allowing truncation of a negative q. ENNReal real powers at zero and at negative exponents have the expected special cases: T015 uses a strictly positive finite δ, while its proof treats zero diameters separately. Finite-diameter conversions are guarded by mesh bounds, and D.toReal is used only after T004/T005 proves D<top. T001 supplies the real-interval normalization used in T016; T017 explicitly constructs an ambient real isometry whose image of I lies in the cylinder, so it does not misapply the Euclidean-only clause of T002 directly to ℝ. The header contains concrete object definitions, no proof-bearing structure fields and no definition assuming the target. These conversions remain proof obligations at assembly, as appropriate for this stage.
